reason: The cited evidence (E2) directly supports the formation of a dense HfO₂ layer, reduced weight gain, and Hf-Zr interdiffusion for a 120 μm Hf coating on a refractory HEA, but it does not address adhesion under thermal cycling, performance on Zr-alloy substrates, or neutron absorption, leaving several key premises unsupported or extrapolated.
premises: A ~120 μm Hf-rich coating can be deposited on a Zr-alloy substrate.
The coating forms a dense, protective HfO₂ scale during high-temperature oxidation.
Interdiffusion between Hf and Zr creates a transition layer that improves adhesion.
The HfO₂ scale significantly reduces oxidation weight gain compared to uncoated material.
The coating remains adherent and resists spallation under high-temperature and cyclic conditions.
